context.title: Victory and a Foolish Treaty
context.summary: God gives Ahab two unexpected victories over Ben-hadad of Syria, but Ahab spares Ben-hadad and makes a treaty with him. A prophet acts out a parable condemning Ahab.
context.background: Syria (Aram), with its capital at Damascus, was Israel's main rival to the northeast in this period. Ben-hadad's advisers assumed Israel's God was a local hill god who would be weak on the plains (v. 23) — a common ancient belief that gods ruled particular territories.

customs.note: Coarse sackcloth and ropes on the head were signs of humble surrender.
Trading quarters or market rights in a foreign capital — a valuable commercial concession.

watchFor: Ahab's proverb: let not him that girds on armor boast like him that takes it off (v. 11).
The prophet's disguise traps Ahab into judging himself (vv. 39–42).

w: and it will strike down you

people.name: Ben-hadad
people.summary: The king of Syria whom Asa, king of Judah, employed to invade Israel (1 Kings 15:18).

people.name: Ahab
people.summary: The son of Omri, whom he succeeded as the seventh king of Israel. His history is recorded in 1 Kings 16-22. His wife was Jezebel, who exercised a very evil influence over him.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: A watch-mountain or a watch-tower. In the heart of the mountains of Israel, a few miles north-west of Shechem, stands the “hill of Shomeron,” a solitary mountain, a great “mamelon.”

places.name: Syria
places.summary: (Heb. Aram), the name in the Old Testament given to the whole country which lay to the north-east of Phoenicia, extending to beyond the Euphrates and the Tigris.

places.name: Aphek
places.summary: A town on the road from Damascus to Palestine, in the level plain east of Jordan, near which Benhadad was defeated by the Israelites (1 Kings 20:26, 30; 2 Kings 13:17).

places.name: Damascus
places.summary: Activity, the most ancient of Oriental cities; the capital of Syria (Isa. 7:8; 17:3); situated about 133 miles to the north of Jerusalem.
